name: Money Laundering Networks
title: Money Laundering Networks
answer: Money laundering networks are groups of individuals and entities that move illicit funds through a series of transactions to hide their origin and ownership. In fraud detection and forensics, the scope covers identifying these networks from financial records, corporate filings, and communication metadata. It includes the classic stages of placement, layering, and integration, as well as modern typologies such as trade-based laundering and the use of virtual assets. The work also involves mapping relationships between accounts, shell companies, and beneficial owners to find the people behind the transactions.

sections.body: Money laundering networks are groups of individuals and entities that move illicit funds through a series of transactions to hide their origin and ownership. In fraud detection and forensics, the scope covers identifying these networks from financial records, corporate filings, and communication metadata. It includes the classic stages of placement, layering, and integration, as well as modern typologies such as trade-based laundering and the use of virtual assets. The work also involves mapping relationships between accounts, shell companies, and beneficial owners to find the people behind the transactions.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on transaction monitoring systems, customer due diligence records, and corporate registries that supply the raw data. Analysts use graph databases to store and query relationships, along with stream processing for real-time alerts and batch systems for historical analysis. The site's 732 AI tools include categories for entity resolution and link analysis, though not all are built for financial crime. Compute is often a mix of on-premises systems for sensitive data and cloud services for scalable graph analytics.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method combines rule-based alerts with network analysis and machine learning. Analysts start with suspicious activity reports and then use graph algorithms to detect communities, central nodes, and unusual paths between entities. Entity resolution links records that refer to the same person or company across different datasets. Human review remains essential to confirm findings and to reduce false positives before any report is filed.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance covers anti-money laundering regulations, know-your-customer rules, data protection laws, and sanctions regimes. The site tracks 223 compliance and regulation pages and 150 active AI lawsuits, and money laundering work sits within that broader compliance and litigation context. Risks include false positives that burden legitimate customers, privacy violations from overbroad data collection, and bias in automated decisions. Provenance matters, so analysts must document data sources, maintain audit trails, and preserve chain of custody for any evidence.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward more automated network detection, with graph neural networks and federated learning gaining attention. Real-time monitoring and privacy-enhancing technologies are being explored to balance speed with data protection. The site tracks 393 merger and acquisition filings, and consolidation among analytics vendors may shape the tools available to investigators. Crypto tracing and cross-border data sharing are likely to remain active areas as laundering methods evolve.
